items.title: Pennsylvania’s Eastern Mississauga is the rattlesnake no one talks about
items.summary: Subscribers are entitled to 10 gift sharing articles each month. These can be shared with friends and family who are not subscribers. Subscribe now! or Sign in to your account. Most Pennsylvanians likely have never heard of the Eastern Mississauga rattlesnake, as this little-known snake lived in a small area of the state’s western region, which is dotted with wetlands. The small-bodied, timid rattlesnake is on the brink of extinction and is both a federally threatened species, first listed in 2016, and a Pennsylvania state-endangered species. The often-spotted Timber Rattlesnake gets most of the public’s attention and mentions in folklore, but the mysterious Mississauga is seldom seen, rarely discussed, and lives a secretive life that even herpetologists struggle to find and study. One of the rarest vertebrates in the Commonwealth and rarest venomous snake, shrinking habitat and increased land development has dramatically increased the pressure on this snake to find a home today. The fact is, the Mississauga does not fit modern landscapes and scientists and land managers are offering some hope and are working urgently to protect what remains of this quiet species. Historically, the Mississauga inhabited a patchwork of marshes, wet open fields and brushy lowlands across the Great Lakes region and into western Pennsylvania. The damp open ground with thick grasses and scattered shrubs, which this snake prefers, was more common in the past, but the 20th Century brought disaster to its habitat with meadows drained and plowed for farming, other suitable areas were mined or developed, fields grew into forests and the widespread construction of roadways and highways fragmented what remained. By the late 1900s, the Mississauga had faded from most of Pennsylvania, and surveys that once yielded regular sightings eventually came up empty of evidence. Today, only a limited number of populations survive, all in the western counties, and even those are small-scale and sporadic.

items.title: Peel Police Data Shows Over 300 Vehicle Thefts Across Mississauga and Brampton in a Single Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police data shows more than 300 vehicles were reported stolen across Mississauga and Brampton over the past month. INsauga reports the count covers the 31-day period from July 22 to August 22, during which 304 vehicle thefts were recorded across the two cities. Of those, the outlet reports 175 thefts occurred in Mississauga and 126 in Brampton, with three additional incidents in Caledon falling under Peel police's jurisdiction. INsauga notes this report differs from some previous releases in that Peel Regional Police did not provide an updated breakdown showing how many of the cases had been solved, remained under investigation or were considered unsolved. The absence of that breakdown, according to the outlet, leaves residents without a clear picture of how much progress investigators have made on any of the reported thefts.

items.title: Mississauga receives $8.7 million in federal funding to support active transportation projects
items.summary: Funding will support improvements along the Culham Trail and construction of a new pedestrian and cycling bridge in Port Credit. 7 million in federal funding for Mississauga through the Government of Canada’s Active Transportation Fund. This investment will support improvements to the Culham Trail and the construction of a new pedestrian and cycling bridge in Port Credit. Together, these projects will improve connections across the city and make it easier for residents to choose active transportation. One of Mississauga’s most popular recreational corridors, the Culham Trail welcomes more than 500,000 visitors annually. Stretching through Erindale Park and Riverwood, the trail connects residents and visitors to natural areas, neighbourhoods and key destinations across the city. The reconstruction project will modernize nearly four kilometres of multi-use recreational trail and enhance flood protection measures. Additional amenities will also be added, such as new seating and an outlook viewing area, a bike share system, upgraded signage and landscaping. A new 65-metre active transportation bridge is being constructed to span the Credit River between Port Credit Memorial Park and the Port Credit Royal Canadian Legion, north of Lakeshore Road. Designed exclusively for pedestrians and cyclists, the bridge will provide a safe, accessible crossing separated from vehicle traffic, linking Port Credit and the GO Station with the Mineola West neighbourhood. The project supports the City’s efforts to enhance transportation options and strengthen connections along the waterfront. Identified as a priority through the Lakeshore Corridor Transportation Improvements study, the bridge advances the vision of the Lakeshore Connecting Communities Master Plan to improve walking, cycling and access to destinations along the Lakeshore corridor.

items.title: Mississauga Deferred a 112-Unit Townhouse Proposal After Residents Flagged 19 Requested Variances
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the city's committee of adjustment has deferred a request to approve a minor variance that would allow construction of a 112-unit stacked townhouse complex on Bloor Street near Riverspray Crescent. The outlet reports the 0.8-hectare site is zoned for residential highrises and currently holds a 17-storey, 323-unit apartment building that would remain on the property alongside the new townhomes. Mississauga.com reports the committee deferred the landowner's request on August 20 after residents raised objections to the plan. Kim Pines of the Applewood Hills and Heights Residents' Association told the outlet her group welcomed the decision, citing legitimate concerns raised by committee members, including the high number of 19 variances being requested, a lack of communication and consultation with the wider community, and worries about increased parking pressure. According to the Residents' Association, the developer has since agreed to hold a community meeting.

items.title: Ontario couple built this dreamy botanical garden that’s home to one of Canada’s largest fountain shows
items.summary: Luxury hotel brands are getting into the cruise business. A … There are more than 260 painted images or pictographs along … The Festival of Fountains is starting its season on Aug. 28. The Festival of Fountains is designed and choreographed by co-owner Darren Heimbecker. About a two-hour drive southwest of Toronto blooms a dreamy botanical destination known as one of Ontario’s premier horticultural gardens. Situated in the Norfolk County hamlet of Wilsonville, Whistling Gardens (698 Concession 3) is run by a local couple who envisioned a peaceful nature sanctuary. Alongside the garden, they created Festival of Fountains — one of Canada’s largest fountain shows that is starting its season on Aug. 28. Co-owner Darren Heimbecker spent much of his childhood with his grandparents while they worked at a greenhouse. That experience inspired a deep desire to build his own botanical garden — a dream he shared with his wife, Wanda, while they were dating. The couple eventually purchased a 56-acre farm featuring an 1881 stone home that had belonged to only two previous families. Transforming a former cornfield into a 20-acre botanical garden, they officially launched Whistling Gardens in 2012. Today, it’s home to North America’s largest peony and conifer collection, while displaying more than 4,500 plants, including the rarest tree in the world, the Baishan fir.

items.title: Christopher Nolan and Denis Villeneuve Have Turned Mississauga's Imax Into Hollywood's Hottest Ticket
items.summary: According to Toronto Star business columnist David Olive, Imax, the Mississauga-based motion picture technology company, is reportedly mulling a sale as its technology becomes the darling of directors such as Christopher Nolan and Denis Villeneuve. Olive writes that this year's most talked-about film, The Odyssey, is the first feature-length movie shot entirely with Imax's 70mm-format cameras, and the immersive experience it delivers alongside the company's most sophisticated projectors and screens is drawing fans hundreds of kilometres to reach one of the 41 Imax screens worldwide fully equipped with its latest technology. The column notes Imax has 1,865 locations across 91 countries, including 43 in Canada, though most of those use traditional digital projection while still carrying the company's trademark floor-to-ceiling, wall-to-wall screens. Major studios including Disney, Paramount and Sony Columbia scramble to book Imax screens for their biggest releases, according to Olive, even though Imax itself does not make movies or operate cinemas. Instead, the Star reports, the company leases its cameras to filmmakers and studios and its screens, projectors and other complex equipment to cinema operators.

items.title: Fourteen Names on the Ballot as Mississauga's Mayoral Race Heads to an October Vote
items.summary: According to INsauga, the field for Mississauga's mayoral race is now set ahead of the October 26 municipal election, with 14 names on the list of candidates seeking to lead Canada's seventh-largest city for the next term of council. INsauga reports the highest-profile contenders are current mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie, who are joined in the race by city councillors Alvin Tedjo of Ward 2 and Dipika Damerla of Ward 7, along with 10 other candidates with varying levels of campaign experience. Crombie left the mayor's office in 2024 after a decade in the role to lead the Ontario Liberals and challenge the premier, and INsauga reports she is now seeking to reclaim the seat because she believes better days are ahead for the city. In a news release cited by the outlet, Crombie said residents she meets consistently raise the same concerns, rising costs of living, safety, and traffic and congestion eating into time with family. She said voters also want assurance that city hall is focused on getting things done, according to INsauga, and that she is running because she believes Mississauga can do better.

items.title: Erindale Cul-de-Sac Home Offers Over 5,200 Square Feet and a Self-Contained Basement Suite
items.summary: According to INsauga's House of the Week feature, this week's pick is a large family home tucked on a quiet cul-de-sac in Mississauga's Erindale neighbourhood, offering more than 5,200 square feet of finished living space designed for multi-generational living. The outlet reports the main floor combines living and dining rooms with a home office, while the kitchen overlooks a breakfast area and a family room finished with built-in cabinetry, a fireplace and backyard views. Upstairs, INsauga notes the home has four bedrooms with vaulted ceilings and custom closets, including a primary suite with dual walk-in closets, a six-piece ensuite bathroom, a fireplace and a sitting area, and the additional bedrooms have their own ensuite bathroom access. The basement, according to the outlet, has its own separate entrance and a self-contained three-bedroom suite complete with two full bathrooms, living areas, a recreation space, a wine cellar and a cold room. INsauga reports the property backs onto a gate leading to the Queensway corridor, giving residents access to nearby walking and cycling trails, Huron Park, a community centre and Trillium Hospital.

items.title: Meteorologists Warn of 80 km/h Wind Gusts as a Stormy Weekend Rolls Into Southern Ontario
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, a stormy weekend is on the way for southern Ontario, with Environment and Climate Change Canada forecasting showers, thunderstorms and wind gusts of up to 80 kilometres an hour across the region on August 22 and 23. The outlet reports 15 to 30 millimetres of rain is expected in most areas, with the worst conditions arriving Saturday in the southwest and Sunday further east, including Ottawa. A sunny Friday will give way to increasing cloudiness overnight as a low-pressure system moves in, according to Mississauga.com, with clouds reaching the Windsor area first before spreading across the rest of southern Ontario. Environment and Climate Change meteorologist Jean-Philippe Begin told the outlet that Toronto could still see some sunny breaks early Saturday morning, but that clouds will move in by late morning, followed by showers and thunderstorms for the rest of the day. Mississauga.com reports Windsor is likely to see showers and thunderstorms for the entire day, while regions further east such as Toronto may not see the wet weather arrive until the afternoon or evening.
